members.name: Abdelslam Taha
bio: Abdelslam Taha is a Sudanese climate resilience and youth empowerment leader based in Egypt, with a background in medicine and over seven years of experience in environmental advocacy, capacity building, and nonprofit leadership. He is the Founder and CEO of YouthClimate Connect (YCC), a U.S.-registered nonprofit organization that equips young leaders across the Global South with the knowledge, tools, and opportunities to drive equitable climate action.

With professional experience spanning partnerships with the National Geographic Society, The Nature Conservancy, the UN Climate Change Secretariat (UNFCCC), and the Global Landscape Forum, Abdelslam has led and managed initiatives addressing freshwater sustainability, climate adaptation, and digital education for youth. His leadership style combines strategic program design, evidence-based advocacy, and grassroots engagement, focusing on creating accessible pathways for young people to contribute to climate solutions within their communities.

A medical graduate from Zagazig University (Egypt), Abdelslam integrates his scientific background with a policy-oriented approach to climate and public health resilience. He has completed over 130 professional courses and leadership programs, including the Google Project Management Professional Certificate and the Aspire Leaders Program.

Abdelslam’s portfolio includes directing the Freshwater Awareness and Conservation (FWAC) program—an initiative that fostered sustainable water management among Sudanese students—and leading Youth Talks on AI, a multi-day workshop exploring how artificial intelligence can support sustainability and education. His projects emphasize intersectional thinking, bridging technology, health, and environmental justice.

Recognized for his leadership and commitment, Abdelslam is a National Geographic Society Seed Grant recipient (2023) and an Aspire Leaders Program graduate (2024). Fluent in Arabic and English, he continues to advocate for Global South representation in international climate discourse. Through his work, Abdelslam envisions a generation of informed, connected, and empowered youth shaping a resilient and equitable future for all.

members.name: Salim Suleiman Sani
bio: Salim Suleiman Sani, is a forward-thinking professional based in Kano State, Nigeria, with a passion for blockchain technology, public policy, and transhumanism. As a dedicated advocate for innovative solutions, he serves as a Fellow at the European Carbon Offset Tokenization Association (ECOTA), where he contributes to discussions on tokenized carbon credits and blockchain's role in achieving net-zero objectives through community participation, working groups, and content creation. He also holds ambassadorships with HP LIFE, The Life Skills as a Talent Ambassador, and Paragon One as a Senior Ambassador, focusing on promoting educational and professional development programs to drive participation and applications.

The Africa Blockchain Institute (ABI), Salim plays a key role in advancing blockchain adoption across the continent, organizing high-impact events such as the Francophone Africa Blockchain Summit, webinars on topics like creating personal DAOs, cybersecurity, and harnessing blockchain for secure healthcare, as well as managing alumni communities through codes of conduct, launch reports, and collaborative partnerships. His work emphasizes inclusivity, ethical engagement, and practical applications of emerging technologies, including explorations into biometric voice authentication, context-aware task chaining, and ambient intelligence.

members.name: Chretianne Gomez
bio: Chretianne is the Media Communications Director at YCC. She is currently finishing her final undergraduate year at UCLA studying Geography/Environmental Studies with minors in GIS and Environmental Systems and Society. She is passionate about sustainability communications, and aims to change the dialogue and sentiment around environmental issues, such as climate change. With this, she hopes to empower youth to engage in climate conversations, and learn how social media and interpersonal interactions shift how groups and organizations achieve sustainability goals.

members.name: Monib Taha Mohamednour
bio: Monib Mohamednour is the Co-Founder and the director of the technology Office at YouthClimate Connect (YCC), where he combines his engineering background and passion for technology to build and maintain an online platform that connects and empowers young people around the world to take meaningful climate action. He oversees the technical development and security of the platform, manages data systems, and ensures a seamless user experience. By collaborating closely with other YCC teams, he helps integrate innovative software solutions that enhance the organization’s digital presence and community engagement.

Originally from Sudan and currently residing in Pennsylvania, United States, Monib also works in the electronics and circuit board manufacturing industry, where he continues to deepen his expertise in technology and systems development. Through his work at YCC, he strives to bridge technology and sustainability to inspire global youth-driven change.

members.name: Isha Shah
members.role: Director of the Climate Education Office
bio: A budding environmental journalist, I am passionate about research, writing and reporting. I am motivated to explore, travel and learn. The intersectionality between social justice, livelihoods and environmental conservation draws me to rural landscapes and to learn and unlearn through experience.The writer in me is interested in storytelling and asks critical questions with the aim to expose systemic failures and injustices. I have worked on story writing, documentation, content creation and reporting that have helped me skill up my writing abilities over the years.

Currently, I work as a Storytelling Fellowship Coordinator with Himal Prakriti—a trust for Nature—and Voices of Rural India. I also work as an Environmental Fellow for Territories of Life—a project supported by Kalpvriksha. Over the course of a year, I have overseen the publication of 30+ stories written by Indian rural storytellers on the Voices of Rural India website and the publication of a book titled 'Baarish ki Pehli Boonde—Stories from Uttarakhand.' I have worked with MappitGIS to document water sources and conduct a detailed water survey in the Munsiari region of Uttarakhand and been involved in the documentation of biodiversity in the Sarmoli Jainti Van Panchayat.

I am Co-founder and Director of the Climate Education Office at YouthClimate Connect (YCC). Together with the CEO and 8 other Co-founders, we established YCC two years ago, to involve youth globally for climate education and action.

An alumnus of Ashoka University, who pursued a major in Psychology, a minor in International Relations, Environmental Science and Media Studies, I am a curious learner. The fact that there is so much out there in the world to explore excites me and keeps me motivated. All my courses at Ashoka have helped me challenge dominant narratives, think critically and engage with ideas holistically.

I also demonstrate skill in Social Media, Training, Teaching, Research, News Writing, Event Management and Project Planning. I am an avid reader and I dabble in both the fiction and non-fiction categories, as both bring me closer to lived experiences. I have also engaged in website design, storytelling, research and fieldwork.

members.name: Ibrahim Mohammed Osman
members.role: Director of Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL)
bio: ​Ibrahim Osman is the Director of Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) at YouthClimate Connect (YCC). He currently oversees the design and enforcement of the entire evidence system for the organization's pivotal 2026 Pilot Year.​As a Co-founder, Ibrahim has served in continuous executive leadership since YCC's inception in 2023. He was the Chief Operating Officer (COO) until early 2025, where he was responsible for building YCC's operational and governance backbone. He then accepted a focused, strategic assignment to lead the MEAL function—the organization's most critical risk mitigation priority.

​Grounded in Data Analytics and his executive experience, Ibrahim ensures the rigor of the entire system. He leverages his expertise— including roles as Data Analytics lead at the Sudan Climate Collective and MEAL Manager at the Women Development and Environment Organization (WDEO) to: 
- ​Design and enforce the YCC MEAL System and Policy. 
​- Guarantee that every program is measurable, compliant, and audit-ready. His current mandate sets the operational standard for the future, ensuring YCC operates with professional rigor and undeniable evidence

members.name: Selena Lopez
bio: Selena has been working with YCC for over 2 years since completing an externship through the National Geographic Society and The Nature Conservancy. Selena is currently a Graduate student at Wayne State University in Michigan, working towards a masters degree in environmental engineering. She works for a small engineering firm designing green infrastructure and storm water for cities. Selena actively volunteers in her community, in the past she has cleaned up roadsides from trash and implemented community garbage cans.

members.name: Kiros Tekeste
bio: Kiros Tekeste is the Coordinator for Partnerships and Development at Youth Climate Connect (YCC), where he leads efforts to build strategic collaborations, mobilize resources, and strengthen youth-led climate action initiatives. With a strong background in management, environmental health, and humanitarian work, he has over five years of experience engaging stakeholders, fostering partnerships, and driving impactful programs in climate advocacy, community resilience, and youth empowerment.

members.name: Joy Okolo
bio: Conveying information and ideas effectively is undeniably essential in transforming a vision into reality. Joy, a Master’s degree holder in English from the University of Lagos, Nigeria, brings that philosophy to life across every space she serves.

She is a seasoned Brand Strategist and Growth Manager working with various firms to shape narratives that drive connection, awareness, and meaningful engagement. Her passion for communication extends beyond brands and ideas into reality and purpose. At YouthClimate Connect (YCC), where she serves as a Media and Communications Coordinator, Joy channels her storytelling expertise to educate, inform, and inspire environmentally conscious actions through creative communication and content.

From an early age, recycling and environmental care have been a personal mission. From gathering plastic waste to clean up her community, to supporting children’s education with proceeds from recycled materials, Joy has always believed in small actions that ripple into larger change.

Over the years, she has deepened her understanding of sustainability and continues to lend her voice and skills. Indeed, her goal is to amplify the world voices, one voice at a time and as much as she can for climate education and advocacy across media platforms and every process of communicating information.
In her words: "To be happy tomorrow, one must be in love with the world today"

members.name: Kidus Yohannes
bio: Kidus Yohannes is a Machine Learning Engineer with experience in developing AI-driven solutions and optimizing search and retrieval systems for faster, more efficient performance. He serves as the National Director of the African Youth Forum International in Ethiopia and has held leadership roles with AIESEC in Ethiopia. Kidus is passionate about applying AI and technology to create social impact and drive community development.

members.name: Raymond Kwame Amachor
bio: Experienced Agricultural Professional, Educator, and Project Coordinator with a passion for driving innovation and sustainable development in agriculture. Proven track record of successfully coordinating projects and fostering collaborative relationships to achieve impactful results. Dedicated to empowering communities through education, research, and community-driven initiatives. Currently serving as Project and Innovation Coordinator at YCC, while leveraging teaching expertise to inspire future generations of leaders.
